clue.text: Rooney's caught Peter out

indicators.note: to catch something is to hear it, so we want a word that is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Wayne Rooney is the England footballer; his first name is what we hear

explanation.surface: A footballer's dismissal of a man called Peter, or a catch he took.
explanation.walkthrough: Rooney's first name, Wayne, sounds just like WANE. Wayne Rooney is a famous English footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: To wane is to dwindle and fade away gradually, the same idea as petering out.

clue.text: 6A is fair game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the answer to 6 across, an uproar or fuss
second meaning: a fairground game of throwing rings over prizes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair game' looks like the idiom for a legitimate target, but here it is a game played at a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a noisy commotion or ballyhoo, and also the ring-tossing stall found at funfairs.

clue.text: Investigators announced to conduct an administrative sell-off

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the sound of the phrase matters, not its spelling

parts.note: private eyes are detectives hired to investigate

explanation.surface: Detectives are called in to run the sale of some public body.
explanation.walkthrough: Say PRIVATE EYES quickly and you get PRIVATISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Privatising means a government selling a state-owned enterprise or service into private ownership.

clue.text: Approaching bad weather wiping out French seat of government

indicators.note: wiping something out erases it, so letters are removed from the weather phrase

parts.note: a storm front is the leading edge of an oncoming storm
Fr is the standard abbreviation for French

explanation.surface: An approaching storm blots out a French government building.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove FR from STORM FRONT to leave STORMONT, the parliament buildings of Northern Ireland in Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormont houses the Northern Ireland Assembly and Executive, so it is the region's seat of government.

clue.text: It's fabulous smashing fascists, left and right

indicators.note: smashing something breaks it to pieces, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone cheers the defeat of fascists from both sides of politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' looks like praise to go with 'fabulous', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: First-class describes something of the highest quality, excellent, which is what fabulous means informally.

clue.text: Uproar of ultimately catastrophic, harmful relationship

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: last letter of catastrophic
last letter of harmful
an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: The fuss surrounding a disastrous, toxic romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' serves both catastrophic and harmful, giving C and L before AMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud, insistent outcry or din, which is what an uproar is.

clue.text: See 20
Like a fruitcake, only more so

definitions.text: Like a fruitcake, only more so

parts.note: surface reading: resembling a cake full of dried fruit and perhaps nuts
setter's reading: a fruitcake is slang for a mad person, so we want the comparative of the word meaning crazy

explanation.walkthrough: Fruitcake is informal for an eccentric or crazy person; a fruitcake can also contain nuts, which is the double sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutty means crazy and also full of nuts; the comparative form describes something even more so.

clue.text: Frank's cycling over my dead body

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the final letter rotates to the front of the word

parts.note: frank and open both mean candid

explanation.surface: A man named Frank refuses outright to go bike riding.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the last letter of OPEN to the front to get NOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Over my dead body is an emphatic refusal, and nope is a casual, firm no.

clue.text: Nick's upset, missing opening of Ukrainian tourist destination

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns a word upside down, so it reads from the bottom up
something missing is absent, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to trouser is slang for pocketing or stealing money, as is to nick

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Ukrainian

explanation.surface: A man called Nick is distressed at losing his way to a Ukrainian holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick reads as a name but is the verb meaning steal. Take U out of TROUSER and turn TROSER round to get RESORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a place people visit for holidays and recreation, a destination for tourists.

clue.text: First bit of stinking blubber to clean up

indicators.note: the first bit of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of stinking
to blubber is to cry noisily

explanation.surface: Clearing away a smelly mass of whale fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' suggests whale fat but is the verb meaning cry.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep is to brush away dirt and debris, tidying a floor or area.

clue.text: Sleuth hides gold in jars and disappears immediately

indicators.note: hiding something means keeping it inside, so the sleuth wraps around the metal
in places that whole group inside the next word

parts.note: first part of VASES, jars or pots
first letter of PI, a private investigator
or is the heraldic word for gold
second letter of PI
rest of VASES

explanation.surface: A detective conceals gold in pots and then vanishes into thin air.
explanation.walkthrough: PI around OR makes PORI, which then goes inside VASES. PI is short for private investigator.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that vaporises turns to vapour and vanishes at once, which is disappearing instantly.

clue.text: Roast meat sat uneasily

parts.note: lamb is a kind of meat

indicators.note: doing something uneasily means being unsettled, so the letters shift out of place

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A joint of roast meat sat there awkwardly on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roast' looks like part of the dinner, but it is the definition, in its sense of criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise them harshly, and lambast means to scold or attack fiercely.

clue.text: City centre has changed under Mayor's lead

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means placed below, so the rearranged letters follow
a lead is what goes first, so take the opening letter

parts.note: first letter of Mayor

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A city's downtown has been transformed under its mayor's leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester is a city in north-west England with an elected mayor, so the surface fits it neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester is a major city in north-west England, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Harmonise with piece of music on curriculum

indicators.note: a piece of something is a section of it, so the answer is a run of letters inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters run from the end of music into the start of curriculum

explanation.surface: Bringing a musical piece into line with what the school syllabus requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of music' looks like a single noun phrase, but 'piece of' is doing the work alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur with someone is to agree with them, being in accord or harmony with them.

clue.text: Arrangement of Grieg sonata at last we'd listened in on

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks a piece, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at last means at the end, so take the final letter

parts.note: last letter of sonata
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Musicians overheard someone's arrangement of a Grieg sonata.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement' plays on the musical sense; it is the anagram signal for all of GRIEG, A and WED.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is British informal for eavesdropping, secretly hearing another person's conversation.

clue.text: Flimsy Trident missiles are kept here, targeted primarily against Bali's interior

parts.note: Britain's Trident nuclear missiles are carried in submarines

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the opening letter

parts.note: first letter of targeted
anti means opposed to

indicators.note: the interior of a word is its middle, so drop the first and last letters

parts.note: the middle letters of Bali

explanation.surface: Nuclear missiles held aboard vessels are aimed at the heart of an Indonesian island.
explanation.walkthrough: Trident is the UK's submarine-launched nuclear missile system, so its missiles sit IN SUBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Insubstantial means lacking solidity or strength, which is what flimsy describes.

clue.text: One lending boxes reserved for acrobat's equipment

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so one word sits inside another

parts.note: uncle is old British slang for a pawnbroker, who lends money against goods
a reserved person can be cool or icy in manner

explanation.surface: A lender packs something set aside for a circus performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like a noun but is the verb. Uncle as slang for a pawnbroker is old British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicycle is a one-wheeled cycle ridden by circus performers and acrobats as part of their act.

clue.text: Have another pull, it's very sore

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to draw again, as a pull is a draw

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' suggests tugging a muscle, which makes 'very sore' feel like a consequence; but pull here means draw.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw is to draw again, and red raw describes skin that is inflamed and painful.

clue.text: Midnight mass?

parts.note: surface reading: the church service held at midnight on Christmas Eve
setter's reading: the middle of the word night is the letter g, the symbol for a metric unit of mass

explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of 'night' is G, and g is the symbol for a gram, so the mid-night letter really is a mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramme is the basic metric unit of mass, a thousandth of a kilogram, written g.

clue.text: The reformed, almost agreeable native

indicators.note: reformed means made over in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: nice means pleasant or agreeable

explanation.surface: A description of a pleasant local person who has changed their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reformed' looks like a group of people, but it is just the word THE rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic can mean relating to a people's own origin or descent, close to native or indigenous.

clue.text: Cowardliness — trait originally cultivated in royal household

indicators.note: cultivated means worked over like soil, so the letters are turned and rearranged
the result is found within the cultivated letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so take the first letter

parts.note: first letter of trait

explanation.surface: Cowardice as a character flaw nurtured within the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: Windsor Castle in Berkshire is one of the British monarch's official residences.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor Castle is a residence of the British royal family, so it houses a royal household.

clue.text: One's excluded from more elegant conversation

indicators.note: excluded from means left out of, so a letter is removed from the following word

parts.note: natty means smart and stylish
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone is shut out of a more refined discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I out of NATTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A natter is British informal for a chat, a casual conversation.

clue.text: Spear a fish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long-shafted infantry weapon
second meaning: a predatory freshwater fish

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an order to harpoon a fish; both nouns are definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a long infantry spear and also a large predatory freshwater fish.

clue.text: Further work of tailor, at ease about finishing touches of fancy apparel

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the others

parts.note: first part of RESTING, relaxing at ease

indicators.note: finishing touches are the last bits, so take the final letters

parts.note: last letters of fancy and apparel
rest of RESTING

explanation.surface: A tailor, relaxing, adds the final flourishes to a fancy outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: RESTING goes around Y and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Restyling is giving clothes a new cut or design, which is additional tailoring work.

clue.text: Bear with me, short of English charm

parts.note: to tote is to carry or bear

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An appeal for patience, as one's English charm falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear with me' reads as a plea for patience, but bear is TOTE. Drop the E of ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or object believed to have protective power, like an amulet or talisman.

clue.text: Creature, early version thereof eating nothing without support

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so a letter goes in
without means lacking, so a section is removed

parts.note: a tadpole is the young form of the creature
a pole is a supporting post
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A creature's ancestor swallowing nothing while it lacks support.
explanation.walkthrough: TADPOLE minus POLE leaves TAD, which takes in O. 'Thereof' points back to the creature itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a warty amphibian, one example among the many animals covered by the general word.

clue.text: Expression of exuberance associated with invention of a bicycle trick

parts.note: whee is a cry of delight
a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A joyful shout linked to someone inventing a stunt on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invention' suggests a new device, but it means a fabrication.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelie is riding a bicycle or motorbike balanced on its back wheel with the front raised, a stunt.

clue.text: Promote variety of vegetables, but not garlic, shallots and broccoli to begin with

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters are mixed up
but not means excluding, so certain letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to begin with means at the start, so take the first letters

parts.note: first letters of garlic, shallots and broccoli

explanation.surface: Pushing a range of vegetables, minus some pungent and green ones.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove G, S and B from VEGETABLES, then rearrange the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate someone is to raise them to a higher rank, the same as giving them promotion.
